title: Erdős #635 OQ-01: Near-Uniqueness of Maximum 1-Admissible Sets

problemStatement.plain: In any maximum 1-admissible set A in {1,...,N}, every element strictly less than N must be odd. The odd set is essentially the unique maximum — the only possible non-odd element is N itself. For odd N, the odd set is the unique optimizer.
whyMatters: Structural characterization of extremal sets beyond cardinality

proven: max_set_interior_odd: all interior elements are odd
unique_max_odd_N: odd set is unique for odd N
open: Full characterization for even N: which even N admit a non-odd maximum set?

insights: Fiber partition via φ(a)=(a-1)/2 is the key structural tool
Even elements in non-last fibers block BOTH next-fiber elements
The blocking mechanism uses two distinct phenomena: diff 1 divides everything, diff 2 divides even numbers
For odd N, uniqueness follows immediately since N is odd too
